FINAL SUBMISSION

**What I changed: nothing — /work/edited is intentionally empty, i.e. the submitted weights are the original starting weights. Every edit I could construct measured at or below the original on accuracy, so the best-supported submission is the unedited model.**

**What I did (key finding).** I diagnosed the dominant failure mode of these weights on MATH-style problems: 34.6% of 512 baseline generations hit the 8,192-token limit (0% correct there), degenerating into a self-sustaining `</think>\n\n</think>…` attractor (154 `</think>` per 1k tokens in cut-offs vs 1.6 in finished answers). I located it mechanistically with teacher-forced attribution (formula validated against the model's own top-k predictions): the MLP adds only ~+2 to the `</think>` logit at spam positions, while the final full-attention layer (L23) adds ~+37 (induction-style copying of the repeating `</think>\n\n` pattern). I built the difference-of-means "close/spam" direction d (cos(d, r</think>)=0.36) and tested targeted edits, all paired ("model": both) on the untouched confirmation sets, 256 generations each:

- L23 o_proj orthogonalized against d (Arditi-style, alpha=-1): select 40.6→35.9 (−4.7pp), longer rambling, more cut-offs. d is entangled with legitimate think-closing; rejected.
- L23 o_proj amplified (alpha=+0.4): −1.6pp on select, MATH 78→70. Rejected (also brushes against the "close thinking early" exclusion).
- Zeroing the spam-selective MLP down_proj columns found by attribution (L23 u218/u234/u41/u66, L19 u343, L14 u7): select 40.6→42.6 (+1.95pp, cut 30.9→23.8, no-boxed 40→29), but this did NOT replicate: confirm_1 46.1→45.3, confirm_2 48.4→45.3; MATH pooled over all three sets: 232/576 edited vs 243/576 original (−1.9pp). The "anti-loop" units also protect normal reasoning (both-finish subset accuracy −3.4pp). Rejected.
- Variants (L23 u218+u234 only; the same extended with next-tier units): both worse or equal; rejected.

**Why I submit original.** No edit I could construct beat the starting weights on problems not used to choose them — the confirmation sets (and MATH-only pooling) all show accuracy ≤ original within noise, and the apparent completion-rate wins (fewer cut-offs, fewer missing boxed answers) did not convert into correct answers (converted cut-off items were only ~39% correct, and editing cost correct finishes elsewhere). Submitting original scores exactly 0 rather than a probable negative.

**Honest assessment and residual risk.** I found no surgical damage: scans of all transformer weights found no exact zeros, no isolated outliers, smooth norm growth across layers, and no anomalous attention or linear-attention parameters; the non-completion failure is mechanistically real but diffuse — L23's induction-style attention write is functionally entangled with the same direction that legitimately closes the thinking section, so it cannot be removed without also suppressing legitimate termination (measured directly: global removal of that direction increased cut-offs and decreased accuracy). I could not locate a cleanly separable component whose repair restores accuracy within this session's budget. If the graders' intended "earlier edit" exists, it is invisible to direct logit attribution and weight-distribution analysis, and/or only repairable by strength-tuning the think-closing pathway globally, which the task excludes (and which measurably traded away math accuracy here). Evidence strength for the submission: it is the empirically safest of 5 measured candidates (original vs 4 rejected edits); expected score is 0, with the submitted weights explicitly documented, notes in /work/notes.md, and no hidden modifications.
